honest self-diagnosis: names both the DRAFT lag and the executed TREE-TUI-PLAN v0.2

the owner's ruling of 2026-08-06 is the authority for the definition, and it is recorded outside this document too — spec/WAL.md `@fact:WAL-C-TUI-IS-DONE-WHEN-THIN`, in the same words: delete it on paper, and if anything but presentation is lost it is not done

the ruling closed a question this repository had left open: the programme of 2026-08-06 listed `what counts as finished for the text interface` among the things NOT decided, as a debt the boss owed the owner
the two rejected measures it names are both real and both measurable in this tree, which is what makes the rejection meaningful rather than rhetorical — see the sibling fact's verdict

the test it borrows really is the flow's own, at the anchor cited: packages/org.vibevm.world/omnichannel/v0.1.0/spec/flows/omnichannel/OMNICHANNEL-PROTOCOL.md:52 — `## What "thin" means, per class {#thinness}`
so the citation resolves and the borrowing is exact rather than a paraphrase: this section applies the flow's general test to one surface instead of inventing a second definition of thinness
and the choice of surface is argued rather than assumed — a TUI is where logic accumulates because rendering and deciding sit in the same event loop

FIRST verdict on this fact — it was written on 2026-08-06 and never judged, which is why the false clause survived a day: the text asserted, of manual tests, `there are none`. That was false when written — spec/manual-tests/ carries MT-01-vibe-tree.md, MT-02-vibe-tree-tui.md and MT-03-vibe-prefs-tui.md, and MT-02 is a substantial visual sign-off for this very subsystem carrying its own marked facts at impl/done. Judging it at the time it was written would have caught it then; that is the argument for the same-pass rule, made by a case rather than by assertion
the clause was corrected in this same landing and the correction is recorded as its own fact rather than silently edited in, so the false reading remains findable
the surviving argument is unaffected and was never the false part: manual tests define no end because their number grows with the screens

the suppression clause, by contrast, reproduces EXACTLY: at the perimeter now stated in this section there are 53 `#[allow(...)]` attribute lines, of which 27 are bare and 26 carry an explanatory trailing comment. Measured 2026-08-06 by `grep -hE '^\s*#\[allow\([^)]*\)\]\s*$'` over the two tui/ trees
and the claim that all 27 could close without the subsystem moving is the point of the rejection: an escape hatch is hygiene, and hygiene is orthogonal to whether logic sits in the right layer
the three files exist: spec/manual-tests/MT-01-vibe-tree.md, MT-02-vibe-tree-tui.md, MT-03-vibe-prefs-tui.md — the whole content of that directory as of 2026-08-06

MT-02 is this subsystem's and is not a stub: its opening fact `@fact:purpose` states that the automated suite proves the model and the rendering functions but cannot drive a real terminal, which is precisely the gap a manual test fills, and its facts are marked impl/done
MT-03 covers the second half of the same perimeter, the prefs TUI — which is exactly the tree this section's own measurement counts
all three numbers reproduce exactly, measured 2026-08-06: 63 files, 18 426 lines, 258 `#[test]` attributes over crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/tree/tui/** plus crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/prefs/tui/**

the perimeter was not stated by the fact and had to be recovered: five candidates were measured and only this one matches. `commands/tree/` alone gives 52 / 13 117 / 169; `tree/tui` alone 43 / 11 171 / 152; `commands/tree/` plus `prefs/tui` 72 / 20 372 / 275; `commands/tree/` minus its build code 50 / 12 485 / 163

that the number is right at exactly one of five candidate perimeters is itself the evidence that the perimeter is the intended one, and it is now written into the section as its own fact so the next reader does not repeat the search

the perimeter it names produces both of this section's quoted numbers and no neighbouring perimeter produces either: 63 / 18 426 / 258 for size, and 53 attribute lines of which 27 bare for suppressions

the exclusion it justifies is real: crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/tree/ carries model.rs, build.rs, build/, host.rs, artifacts.rs, diagnostics.rs and plain.rs beside the tui/ subtree — that is the library half, and counting it into a thinness audit would measure the thing the audit is supposed to find OUTSIDE the surface
the two contrast figures quoted in the fact are the measurements above, taken the same day and reproducible with `find`
the law it claims identity with is in this same document, one section down: `@fact:LAYERING-LAW` — `styling never leaks into control or app logic, and vibevm logic never leaks into the app`

the identity holds under inspection rather than by assertion: `vibevm logic never leaks into the app` forbids a specific direction of leakage from inside, and the deletion test detects the residue of that same leakage from outside. One rule, two vantage points
this matters practically, not stylistically: it means the thinness audit does not introduce a second standard the subsystem must satisfy — it is a way of checking the one it already declares

The field list the anchor governs is unchanged; only the provenance sentence moved.

the plan is resolved from the registry section itself: crates/vibe-registry/src/index_client/auth.rs `IndexAuth::for_registry(reg, base_url)` reads `reg.auth` and, under `TokenEnv`, the token from `reg.resolve_token_env_name()` — the same accessor crates/vibe-registry/src/multi_registry_resolver/mod.rs already uses for the git side
no new configuration key exists: `RegistrySection` in crates/vibe-core/src/manifest/project.rs is unchanged, still seven fields, and no second token file is read anywhere

all three construction sites pass it: multi_registry_resolver/mod.rs, crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/search.rs and crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/search/purl.rs each build the plan from the section they already hold

measured before the build, on the pre-change file: `IndexClient` held exactly `file_base` and `server_base`, both URLs, and `build_client` set only a user-agent and a timeout — no header, no credential, at any of the five request sites

and the read path is load-bearing rather than incidental: PROP-005's own query path makes `<base>/by-name/<name>.json` the FIRST network call of a short-name install, so an index that refuses anonymous reads breaks the resolution it exists to accelerate

the header is attached through the client's `default_headers` at the single chokepoint crates/vibe-registry/src/index_client/mod.rs `build_client`, so every request carries it without any URL being rewritten

the contrast is real and in the tree: crates/vibe-registry/src/git_package_registry/auth.rs `inject_token` builds `https://x-access-token:<TOKEN>@…` because git consumes a credential that way — and that same function's doc records the discipline this fact generalises, that the credentialed string must not be logged

gate one: crates/vibe-registry/src/index_client/auth.rs `IndexAuth::plan` returns `None` for `(TokenEnv, Some(token), false)` — a resolved token over a non-https base produces no bearer. Covered by `plan_token_env_http_with_token_is_none`

gate two: crates/vibe-registry/src/index_client/mod.rs `attaches_authorization(base_url, auth)` requires `https://` at the moment of attachment, and `build_client` consults it. Covered by `authorization_attaches_only_for_a_bearer_plan_over_https`, whose four rows are the whole truth table

the sidestep the second gate closes is concrete rather than theoretical: `IndexAuth::Bearer`, `BearerToken::new` and `IndexClient::at_with_auth` are all public, so `at_with_auth("http://…", Bearer(...))` reached the wire before it. Covered from the outside too, by `bearer_plan_over_http_base_sends_no_authorization_header` and its probe twin

recorded because it cost a review round: the first implementation carried only gate one and justified it by analogy to `inject_token` — an analogy that argues the other way, since that function checks the scheme inside itself where no caller can sidestep it

the plan for both regimes is `IndexAuth::HttpIncapable`, carrying the regime's own name — crates/vibe-registry/src/index_client/auth.rs, covered by `plan_ssh_is_http_incapable` and `plan_credential_helper_is_http_incapable`
no header is sent under them: `header_map` returns `None` for every non-bearer plan, covered by `header_map_is_none_for_non_bearer_plans`

and the 401/403 becomes an actionable error rather than a bare status: `IndexError::AuthIncapable` names the regime and the repair (declare `auth = "token-env"`), raised by `classify_failure`. Covered end to end by `ssh_plan_401_surfaces_auth_incapable_error` and `ssh_plan_403_also_surfaces_auth_incapable`

the claim that these regimes cannot answer an HTTP GET is not an assumption about the code but about the mechanisms: this document's own matrix routes `ssh` to ssh-agent and `credential-helper` to git's helper subsystem, neither of which is reachable from a bare `reqwest` request
the outcome type is now three-valued: `ProbeOutcome::{Found, Absent, Refused}` in crates/vibe-registry/src/index_client/mod.rs, where the pre-change signature was `Option<IndexClient>`
the distinction is asserted rather than described: `probe_refused_401_is_distinguishable_from_absent` and `probe_absent_on_404_is_not_refused`

it reaches the operator through a channel that already existed: crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/search.rs and search/purl.rs put the reason into `UnreachableRegistry.reason`, replacing the previous generic `probe of …/repomd.json failed (server down or wrong URL)`; the resolver logs it at warn
and the silent fall-through is deliberately preserved for everything else — 404, connect failure, 5xx still yield `Absent`, so a registry with no index behaves exactly as it did

`BearerToken` in crates/vibe-registry/src/index_client/auth.rs implements `Debug` by hand as `BearerToken(<redacted>)`, has no `Display`, and its only reader `secret()` is private to that module and consumed solely by `header_map`

the redaction survives the whole chain, which is the part worth testing rather than reading: `bearer_token_debug_redacts_secret`, `index_auth_debug_redacts_bearer`, and `index_client_debug_redacts_bearer_token` — the last asserting the derived `Debug` of the client itself neither prints the secret nor omits the redaction marker
and no error variant formats it: `IndexError::AuthIncapable` carries the regime name and the status, never the token
